patch_description: The greedy push heuristics plateau at 2.42 because each circle only moves in crude discrete directions. A proper continuous optimizer can do much better. I add an SLSQP (scipy) refinement stage that directly maximizes the sum of radii as a smooth function of the circle centers: at any fixed center configuration, the optimal radii are given by the exact Gauss-Seidel growth, and the objective is differentiable almost everywhere. I parameterize variables as the 2n center coordinates, and compute radii via a fast inner fixed-point loop (a smooth soft-min can be used, but the fixed point of the hard max is what we want; SLSQP handles the nonsmoothness reasonably if we instead use a smooth log-sum-exp lower bound with inequality constraints r_i + r_j <= d_ij and r_i <= wall). Concretely: variables = (x, y, r) for all circles (3n = 78 vars), objective = -sum(r), constraints: r_i + r_j <= dist for all pairs, and r_i <= min-distance-to-walls. This is a standard formulation of the packing problem and SLSQP handles it well locally, given a feasible starting point from the current best. We run it on the top few candidates and the final result, keeping the best valid output. Validity is preserved because we shrink radii at the end by a small safety margin and re-verify with the exact grow_radii, which is always feasible by construction. To keep eval time bounded, we use the top 3 seeds plus the void-filled result, with a limited iteration budget.
